headline: A rough night on Wall Street dragged everything lower — NASDAQ fell 2.6% last night, MSFT took the biggest hit in your portfolio, and Apple's big AI reveal is the story of the day.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had the worst night of your US holdings, dropping 2.65% last night. No specific negative news, but the broader tech sell-off was brutal — the NASDAQ fell 2.6% and MSFT tends to move with the herd. It's also possible some investors rotated out of MSFT after Apple's big AI announcements, which showed Apple leaning on Google (not Microsoft) as a key AI partner.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI closed down 1.22% today. Your AI ETF tracks global AI companies, and the overnight NASDAQ sell-off filtered through to ASX-listed tech-focused ETFs. The Apple AI news is a longer-term positive for the AI sector, but didn't cushion today's session.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.57% last night as tech broadly sold off. There's some buzz that a GTA 6 Trailer 3 could drop soon, which is a potential catalyst for the stock — but for now the market-wide pressure outweighed any excitement around that.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara edged down 0.85% today. Lithium stocks remain under pressure as the market debates whether the recent lithium price recovery has legs. Overseas policy tightening and a pullback from recent highs have created a tug-of-war between bulls and bears on lithium right now.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG dipped 0.8% today, largely reflecting the overnight US sell-off flowing through into ASX pricing. As a diversified growth fund with heavy US and global equity exposure, it mirrors big moves in offshore markets.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS fell 0.71% today — its pricing on the ASX reflects last night's US market losses, where the S&P 500 dropped 1.58%. VTS tracks the entire US sharemarket, so a broad sell-off like last night flows straight through.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google dipped 0.65% last night, which was actually one of the better performances among tech stocks in a rough session. Interestingly, Apple announced it's partnering with Google for its most advanced AI model — that's a vote of confidence in Google's AI capabilities and could be a quiet tailwind going forward.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL barely moved today, down just 0.11%. However, oil (WTI crude) fell sharply last night — down 3.69% to $87.93 — which is worth watching. Your energy ETF tracks global energy companies, so sustained oil price falls would eventually weigh on it.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE was basically flat today, down just 0.03%. Emerging markets have held up relatively well compared to US equities lately, and this tiny move reflects that resilience. No major catalysts today.

watch_today.title: MSFT: Hold — sharp drop but no fundamental break
watch_today.detail: Microsoft fell 2.65% last night as part of a broad NASDAQ sell-off (-2.6%). There's no company-specific bad news driving this — it's market-wide pressure. MSFT is currently sitting about 9.5% below what you paid, which stings, but the long-term AI and cloud story is intact. No reason to sell into a panic drop.

watch_today.title: GOOG: Hold — Apple partnership is a quiet positive
watch_today.detail: Google only fell 0.65% last night — much less than the rest of tech — and Apple just confirmed it's partnering with Google for its most advanced AI model as part of the new Siri AI rollout. That's a meaningful revenue and credibility signal for Google's AI division. You're up 24% on this position. Hold.

watch_today.title: Oil fell nearly 4% last night — watch FUEL.AX this week
watch_today.detail: WTI crude oil dropped $3.37 (3.69%) last night to $87.93 a barrel. FUEL.AX barely budged today (down 0.11%), but energy company shares tend to follow oil prices with a lag. If oil keeps falling, expect FUEL to feel it. Nothing to act on yet, but keep an eye on oil prices this week.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX: Hold — lithium still in limbo
watch_today.detail: Pilbara slipped another 0.85% today. Lithium prices are in a push-pull: there are signs of a quiet revival, but overseas policy tightening and a pullback from recent highs are keeping a lid on things. You're down 13% on this position. It's a bumpy hold, but selling now locks in the loss — wait for a clearer signal.

watch_today.title: Apple's Siri AI overhaul — big news for GXAI.AX and GOOG
watch_today.detail: Apple unveiled a completely rebuilt Siri powered by advanced AI, and confirmed partnerships with Google and Nvidia for its most powerful AI model. This is a major validation of the AI investment theme — good background news for your GXAI.AX ETF even if it couldn't stop today's sell-off. Hold and let the theme play out.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Hold — GTA 6 Trailer 3 rumours building
watch_today.detail: Take-Two dropped 1.57% last night in the broad sell-off, but there's growing chatter that a GTA 6 Trailer 3 could drop very soon, with fresh evidence surfacing online. If that lands this week, TTWO could pop sharply. Worth watching — you're down about 9.75% on this position so a catalyst like this would be welcome.

markets.summary: Last night was a rough one for US markets — the NASDAQ dropped 2.6% and the S&P 500 fell 1.58%, dragging most tech stocks lower. Oil had the worst night of the lot, crashing nearly 4% to under $88 a barrel. Gold also slid 1.3%. The Aussie dollar dipped slightly against the USD to 70.2 cents. The ASX 200 close data wasn't available in today's feed, but the ASX absorbed the offshore pressure reasonably well given how modest most of the local ETF moves were.

politics.summary: The big domestic story continues to be interest rates — NAB has now updated its forecast and expects a rate cut, while the RBA is defending its past hikes. Separately, the NDIS bill is making contentious progress through Parliament.

stories.title: NAB updates forecast, now expects interest rate cut
stories.why_it_matters: NAB — one of Australia's Big Four banks — has officially changed its forecast and now expects the Reserve Bank to cut interest rates. This follows a string of signals that rate hikes have done enough work. If NAB is right, mortgage holders could see relief soon, and it's generally good news for growth assets like shares and property. Keep an eye on the next RBA meeting for confirmation.

stories.title: One of Australia's biggest banks says interest rate pain is over – for now
stories.why_it_matters: SMH is reporting that a major Australian bank believes the interest rate hiking cycle has peaked — at least for now. This aligns with NAB's updated forecast and suggests the broader banking sector is shifting its view. For borrowers, this is a sign that monthly repayments may not rise further, and could eventually fall. For investors, lower rates ahead tend to support share prices.

stories.title: RBA defends rate hikes: 'Other countries would kill for our problems'
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank is pushing back against criticism of its rate hiking campaign, with a spokesperson arguing Australia's economic performance is actually strong by global standards. The RBA's position is essentially: yes, rates hurt, but inflation is being tamed and employment has held up better than in most comparable countries. This suggests the RBA isn't in a rush to cut and will want to see more data before acting.

stories.title: Six of the most contentious parts of the NDIS bill
stories.why_it_matters: The Federal Government's NDIS reform bill is moving through Parliament and the ABC has outlined the six most hotly contested elements. The NDIS (National Disability Insurance Scheme) supports hundreds of thousands of Australians with disabilities, and any changes to eligibility, funding caps, or support categories affect both participants and the broader government budget. No article text was available, so specific details of the six contested points aren't confirmed here.

ai.summary: Apple dominated the AI news cycle today with a full Siri overhaul and a surprise partnership with Google and Nvidia. Meanwhile, Trump's White House is reportedly drafting an executive order that could reshape how US AI companies — including Google and OpenAI — launch new models.

stories.title: Apple introduces Siri AI — a profoundly more capable personal assistant
stories.why_it_matters: Apple has revealed a completely rebuilt Siri at WWDC 2026 as part of its 'next generation of Apple Intelligence'. The new Siri can understand context across your entire device — apps, emails, messages, photos — and take actions on your behalf without you having to switch between apps. Think of it as Siri finally becoming the genuinely useful assistant it always promised to be. This is Apple's biggest AI push yet and directly competes with Google Assistant and Microsoft Copilot.

stories.title: Apple partnering with Google and Nvidia for most advanced AI model
stories.why_it_matters: CNBC reports Apple is teaming up with Google and Nvidia — not just OpenAI — to power its most advanced AI features. Google's AI models (Gemini) will be available inside Apple devices, meaning Google gets a massive new distribution channel for its AI. This is a big deal for your GOOG holding — Apple has over 1 billion active iPhone users worldwide. Nvidia's chips likely underpin the backend infrastructure. This validates both companies' AI strategies in a big way.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: The Trump administration is reportedly drafting an executive order (a directive the President can issue without Congress) that would impose new requirements on how AI companies test and release powerful models. If it passes, companies like Google (Gemini), OpenAI (ChatGPT), and Anthropic (Claude) may need government sign-off or safety certification before launching major new AI models. For investors in AI-heavy companies, regulation adds uncertainty — but it could also entrench larger, well-resourced players and shut out smaller competitors.

stories.title: The Great American Artificial Intelligence Act — what it means for AI regulation
stories.why_it_matters: A proposed 'Great American AI Act' in the US Congress would set nationwide rules for AI development, cybersecurity obligations, and oversight of AI developers. Right now US AI regulation is patchy — different states are doing different things — so a federal law would standardise the rules. Big tech companies like Google and Microsoft have enough legal teams and resources to comply; smaller startups would struggle more. No article text was available so specific provisions aren't confirmed here.

sport.summary: NRL Round 15 team lists are out with the Broncos heading to Accor Stadium Thursday night. AFL's Big Freeze at the Lake raised money for MND research and delivered some great footy moments. Plus a Gold Coast Suns trade update worth knowing about.

stories.title: NRL 2026 team lists: Every club's confirmed lineup for Round 15
stories.why_it_matters: Round 15 kicks off Thursday night with Rabbitohs vs Broncos at Accor Stadium (7:50 PM). The full team lists are now confirmed across all clubs. On the Gold Coast front, Wests Tigers host the Titans at Leichhardt Oval on Sunday 4:05 PM — a game that matters for Titans fans tracking their season. Seven clubs are on bye this round including Panthers, Storm, and Sea Eagles.

stories.title: Big Freeze had drama, brilliance and freewheeling footy — Neale Daniher would have loved it
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL's annual Big Freeze at the Lake event — where coaches and celebrities slide into icy water to raise money for Neale Daniher's MND (motor neurone disease) charity — went ahead with drama, brilliant football moments, and a big crowd. The Guardian called it the kind of spectacle Daniher himself would have loved. No specific scores were available in the article text, but it was clearly a memorable event both on and off the field.

stories.title: AFL whispers: Gold Coast trade domino as MAJOR trade update unveils
stories.why_it_matters: There's a trade domino forming involving the Gold Coast Suns according to Yahoo Sports Australia. A major trade update has surfaced that could set off a chain of list moves affecting multiple clubs. No article text was available to confirm specific player names or clubs involved, but Gold Coast fans should keep an eye on this one as the mid-season trade period heats up.

stories.title: Umpire Hayden Kennedy earns AFL Hall of Fame nod — 5 Grand Finals, 495 games
stories.why_it_matters: AFL umpire Hayden Kennedy has been inducted into the AFL Hall of Fame, recognised for a career spanning 495 games and 5 Grand Finals. Kennedy is regarded as one of the greatest umpires in the game's history. It's a nice acknowledgement that the men and women who officiate the game — often the most criticised figures in footy — deserve their moment of recognition too.
